status: Reviewed shared bulk assignments implemented; scoped SQL/Core/build and installed phone/tablet acceptance. Wider rank 6/Px remains open.

implementation.entry: Shared selection menu on iOS; independently owned Task menu, list menu and inspector on Mac. Mixed/personal/nested/cross-team input is not partially admitted.
implementation.directory: Frozen opening source/admission; one recipient catalog per distinct project per refresh; intersect all eligible recipients; refresh again on teammate choice. Missing/foreign/stale catalogs never create a review.
implementation.offline: Unassigned and captured actor work without a directory. A previously reviewed identity can remain a frozen intent on connectivity loss. Confirmed eligibility loss in any refreshed project takes precedence over later connectivity loss.
implementation.privacy: Directory and display names are transient; only chosen identity enters the existing guarded edit batch. Invalidation clears directory and cancels remaining project reads; late replies cannot review.
implementation.review: Every selected task and chosen teammate/You/Unassigned appears before final Save. Back returns to choices; Cancel makes no change; already-correct members remain in the cohort.
implementation.transaction: New source migration extends existing private planning allowlist only. Recipient values are validated before casts; canonical Auth recipient locks precede team/project/task locks. Every member delegates live recipient role/ban checks to the existing guarded editor inside one transaction.
implementation.retryUndo: Exact receipts acknowledge original work without reassignment after a recipient leaves/is banned. Whole-group linked Undo restores each member’s original recipient with fresh identities. Sparse optional assignment values clear to explicit null; original frozen source rows are not padded.
implementation.preservation: Unselected tasks, notes, plans, deadlines, estimates, checklist/discussion and unknown task fields stay intact.

result.name: auth_rls_initplan
result.title: Auth RLS Initialization Plan
result.description: Detects if calls to `current_setting()` and `auth.<function>()` in RLS policies are being unnecessarily re-evaluated for each row
result.detail: Table `public.projects` has a row level security policy `fixture_project_access` that re-evaluates current_setting() or auth.<function>() for each row. This produces suboptimal query performance at scale. Resolve the issue by replacing `auth.<function>()` with `(select auth.<function>())`. See [docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security#call-functions-with-select) for more info.

diagnostics: Initial native test queried Riley Chen as an independent static text. The row combines its accessibility children. Scoped descendant-label matching verifies the actual announced row content without changing product accessibility.

The next native pass reached successful Save but compared Undo against an omitted nullable assignment key byte-for-byte. Undo correctly stores explicit null. Final assertions permit only that chosen nullable-field normalization; every unrelated field and unselected row must match exactly, including after relaunch. The sparse Core test now verifies this wire/local distinction.

Code review found that confirmed ineligibility in an early project could be obscured by a later network error and cached-choice fallback. The final picker stops immediately on confirmed loss; a new Core regression proves no review/application and no further project read.

Failed-suite collectors PID 13863 (initial phone) and PID 14996 (intermediate tablet) stayed alive after every test finished. Exact owned commands were verified, then only those collectors received SIGTERM (143). Initial phone xcresult lacked Info.plist and could not export a summary; its log is retained and no green result is claimed. Other failed runs remain diagnostic only.
hostIsolation: Feature sources match the verified candidates apart from reserved App Group/bundle/config and existing Mac debug-fixture/UTType identity substitutions. Each repository owns its code, migration, tests and build inputs; no cross-repository build dependency.

references.finding: Reviewed current breaking-change entries; TLS cipher deprecation does not alter these isolated SQL contracts.
Private privileged helper retains pinned search_path and explicit role grants; public entry remains the existing invoker wrapper.
